page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. The host utilizes an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 16 shared vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 192 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation ratio of 12 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs offering a combined total of 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and comes with no bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data.

In compute and memory evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong execution speed. Single-core processing reaches the top tier, scoring 4201.19 in stress-ng and 2477.0 in Geekbench single-core testing, supported by modern vector instruction flags including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI. Multi-core performance is in the upper quartile, registering 67272.45 on stress-ng and 17385.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 314.07 GB/sec for uncached reads and 145.75 GB/sec for writes. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference benchmarks record 3971.95 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M models and 37.02 tokens per second for generation on 7B parameter models, though throughput reduces on 70B models to 3.91 tokens per second during generation.

The resource balance pairs substantial system memory and 96 GB of aggregate GPU memory against a moderate 16-vCPU footprint. Because local storage is absent, disk I/O performance relies entirely on remote block storage configurations, representing an architectural consideration for data-intensive setups. The configuration is suited for AI inference, small-to-midsize model fine-tuning, computer vision processing, and memory-heavy scientific computing simulations requiring dual GPU parallelization.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-focused cloud instance featuring 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 192 GB of system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by dual NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering an aggregate 96 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results position the server in the top decile for single-core tasks like stress-ng (4201.19) and Geekbench (2477.0), alongside top-quartile multi-core compute and high memory bandwidth of 314.07 GB/sec for uncached reads. LLM inference shows rapid throughput on small to medium models, such as 389.1 text generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. The configuration provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. This server is suited for machine learning inference, distributed graphics workloads, batch data transformations, and memory-intensive GPU compute tasks.
